Strategy doc M6-in-detail confirms M6's own close mood is 'practitioner fluency' ('I know how to test, I know how to learn, I know how to encode', content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md L475) — this opener's permission-giving mood is deliberately distinct from, and does not claim, that closer mood.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer L78 (current): 'In-room opener for M6. Lands before the exercise; permission-giving, not credibility-performance.' Harm the rule guards against: a naming-a-pattern-just-lived closer told BEFORE the student has lived the pattern reads as an abstract claim rather than recognition. That harm is absent here for a structural reason distinct from the ordinary closer case: this memo does not narrate a pattern the STUDENT just lived — it narrates the author's own session, a session the student has not run and is about to. The rule's own placement diagnostic offers a second category for exactly this shape: 'Demo lectures showing a ceiling go at beginning' — a fuller, more rigorous instance of the discipline (subagents, verifier, three-persona sim, source-verify) shown before the student runs their own lighter version. Maintainer's 'Design constraint (session turn 8)' note (current L92) makes the same distinction explicitly: 'Meta-failure (curriculum generation drifting...) is not student-run failure (packaged run drifts at hour 2...). Same condition, different domain.' The close (L53, current) hands off forward ('The next hour you will diagnose gaps in the M5 packaged session...') rather than naming anything already done — a closer-shaped violation would instead gesture backward at the student's own just-finished work. Placement diagnostic result: showing a ceiling in a neighbouring domain, not naming a pattern the reader already lived — opener-shaped by the rule's own carve-out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Five ## headers, current line numbers, all unique, none shared: L9 'The numbers', L15 'Things that went sideways', L31 'The generalisation', L43 'Then I compounded the session', L51 'What the loop is for'. Squint test: 'The numbers' names the concrete content (a session tally); body beneath (L11) is exactly that. 'Things that went sideways' names the section's shape (a seven-paragraph catalogue of named, evidenced incidents, current L17-29 — down from eight after commit 396502f5 cut the duplicate-formula platform-fact paragraph). 'The generalisation' sets up the three standalone thesis sentences immediately below it (L33-39). 'Then I compounded the session' is declarative, backed by L45 ('I moved them into skills that block done'). 'What the loop is for' argues a claim, backed by L59 ('Your job is not to stop the drift. Your job is to catch it and encode what you learned.'). Truth clause: no category errors, no dropped qualifiers, no unsupported universals in any header. No em-dashes (#14 inherit); no empty-container headers ('The move', 'The names'); no orphan mystery/mood headers; no orientation-only headers.
